feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. The evidence is iterations 1, 4, 6 and 10, which used the same geometry and controller and each scored 69.3241, so this design is the reproducible reference. Geometry changes lowered the score: 16 mm footprint in iteration 2 (54.45), y = 0.03 m in iteration 3 (59.64) and the ±0.04 m span in iteration 5 (52.47). Controller changes also lowered it: base_speed 1.15 in iteration 7 (61.77), kd 0.4 in iteration 8 (56.44) and kd 0.2 in iteration 9 (63.59). Line loss has stayed at about 1 per run through every design tested, so the layout is mapped and the controller is at a local optimum for the values tried. Hold the geometry. Body width does not move the off-track limit, which is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 m across the allowed range, so it is not a lever. This is the final iteration, so no further geometry change will be raced.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration 1 geometry unchanged: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m, y = 0.05 m, with wheel, body and mass values as they are.
Do not move the forward offset (y = 0.03 m cost about 10 points in iteration 3) or the footprint (16 mm cost about 15 points in iteration 2) without a controller-based reason.

If a further iteration is ever run, test line-loss handling (search_left or search_right in place of last_direction) as a single controller change, since it is the only untested lever with a clear line-loss link.
